turns.input: How much does it cost to withdraw money?
turns.reply: The first withdrawal each calendar month is free; any additional bank‑wire withdrawal in the same month costs 10 USD, while card and e‑wallet withdrawals have no Aurelia fee and cryptocurrency withdrawals only incur the network fee passed through at cost[1].
sources: Fees and Charges > Withdrawal fees

turns.input: What is the maximum leverage on EUR/USD for a retail client?
turns.reply: The maximum leverage a retail client can use on EUR/USD is 1:30 [1].
sources: Margin and Leverage > Maximum leverage for retail clients

turns.input: What leverage do I get on bitcoin CFDs?
turns.reply: For cryptocurrency CFDs, including Bitcoin, Aurelia offers a maximum leverage of 1:2 for retail clients[1].
sources: Margin and Leverage > Maximum leverage for retail clients

turns.input: At what margin level does stop-out happen?
turns.reply: Stop‑out occurs when the margin level falls to 50%, at which point the platform automatically closes positions to bring the margin level back above that threshold [1][2].
sources: Margin and Leverage > Margin level, margin call and stop-out
UAE Retail CFD Protections > Automatic close-out at 50%

turns.input: When do I get a margin call?
turns.reply: You receive a margin‑call warning when your margin level drops to 100 % (equity divided by used margin) [1].
sources: Margin and Leverage > Margin level, margin call and stop-out

turns.input: What's the commission on the Raw account?
turns.reply: The Raw account charges a commission of 3.50 USD per lot per side, which equals 7.00 USD per round‑turn lot [2].
sources: Fees and Charges > Trading costs by account type

turns.input: Which documents do you accept as proof of address?
turns.reply: Proof of address can be a utility bill or bank statement dated within the last 3 months that shows your full name and residential address [1]. For UAE residents, acceptable proof of address also includes a DEWA, SEWA, ADDC or other UAE utility bill, a telecom bill from Etisalat or du, a bank statement (within 3 months), or a tenancy contract registered with Ejari that is valid on the upload date [2].
sources: Account Verification (KYC) > Documents we accept
UAE Account Opening and Verification > Documents for UAE residents

turns.input: How long does verification take?
turns.reply: Most documents are reviewed within 1 to 2 business days, while enhanced due‑diligence for Tier 3 accounts can take up to 5 business days [2].
sources: Account Verification (KYC) > How long verification takes

turns.input: Why was I charged triple swap on Wednesday?
turns.reply: Swap on Wednesday is charged three times to cover the weekend, so you see a triple swap charge for positions held overnight that day [2].
sources: Fees and Charges > Swap (overnight financing)

turns.input: Is there an inactivity fee?
turns.reply: Yes, if an account has no trading activity for 12 consecutive months while still holding a balance, Aurelia charges an inactivity fee of 10 USD per month until the account becomes active again or the balance reaches zero [1].
sources: Fees and Charges > Inactivity fee

turns.input: Do you charge anything for currency conversion on deposits?
turns.reply: Aurelia does not charge a fee for the deposit itself, but if the deposit currency differs from your account’s base currency a conversion fee of 0.5 % of the converted amount is applied [1][2].
sources: Fees and Charges > Currency conversion
Fees and Charges > Deposit fees

turns.input: Can I lose more than the money I deposited?
turns.reply: Retail clients cannot lose more than the money they have deposited, as negative‑balance protection limits losses to the funds in their trading account and any negative balance is reset to zero[1][2]. Professional clients do not have this protection.
sources: UAE Retail CFD Protections > You cannot lose more than your account balance
Margin and Leverage > Negative balance protection

turns.input: If I ask to take my money out at 4pm, when does it actually get processed?
turns.reply: Withdrawal requests made after the 14:00 server‑time cut‑off, such as a 4 pm request, are not processed the same day; they are processed on the next business day [1].
sources: Deposits and Withdrawals > Withdrawal processing

turns.input: Do you have swap-free accounts, and how are they charged?
turns.reply: Yes, Aurelia offers Islamic (swap‑free) accounts, which do not charge or pay any overnight swap on positions held past the 22:00 server‑time rollover [1]. Instead, for forex positions held longer than three nights a flat administration fee of USD 4 per lot per night is applied, while positions closed within three nights incur no fee [3].
sources: Islamic (Swap-Free) Accounts > What a swap-free account is
Islamic (Swap-Free) Accounts > Administration fee on longer positions

turns.input: How long do you take to respond to a complaint?
turns.reply: Aurelia acknowledges a complaint within 2 business days and provides a final written response within 15 business days; if more time is required, we will inform you before the deadline and the response will never be later than 35 business days [1]. The same timeline applies to UAE clients, with the ticket logged immediately, acknowledgment within 2 business days and an answer within 15 business days [2].
sources: Complaints Policy > What happens next

turns.input: Can UAE residents verify with an Emirates ID?
turns.reply: Yes, UAE residents can verify their identity using a valid Emirates ID (front and back) together with a passport, or they can use UAE Pass instead of uploading the Emirates ID images[1].
sources: UAE Account Opening and Verification > Documents for UAE residents

turns.input: Who regulates Aurelia in the UAE?
turns.reply: Aurelia Markets serves UAE clients through an on‑shore UAE entity that is supervised by the UAE Capital Market Authority (CMA) [1]. Since the entity is on‑shore, it is not regulated by the DFSA or FSRA, which oversee firms in the DIFC and ADGM respectively [2].
sources: UAE Regulation and Client Money > Who regulates Aurelia in the UAE
UAE Regulation and Client Money > Financial free zones: DIFC and ADGM

turns.input: Is Aurelia licensed by the SCA?
turns.reply: Yes, Aurelia Markets is regulated in the UAE by the UAE Capital Market Authority (CMA), which was previously called the Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA); licences issued under the SCA remain valid [2].
sources: UAE Regulation and Client Money > Who regulates Aurelia in the UAE

turns.input: Is my money kept separate from Aurelia's own money?
turns.reply: Yes, your money is kept separate from Aurelia’s own money. Client funds are held in segregated bank accounts licensed in the UAE and are not used for the firm’s business or to pay its creditors, with daily reconciliations and annual independent audits [2]. This segregation protects your money if Aurelia becomes insolvent, though it does not cover trading losses [1].
sources: UAE Regulation and Client Money > What segregation does and does not protect
UAE Regulation and Client Money > How your money is protected

turns.input: How quickly is a local AED bank transfer credited?
turns.reply: Local AED transfers received before 13:00 Gulf Standard Time on a UAE business day are credited the same day; transfers received after that time are credited on the next business day[1].
sources: UAE Regulation and Client Money > Deposits and withdrawals in AED

turns.input: I closed my account. Can you delete all my documents right away?
turns.reply: I’m sorry, but we can’t delete all of your documents immediately. Under anti‑money‑laundering regulations we must retain identity documents and transaction records for at least five years after an account is closed, and those records cannot be removed before that period ends [3]. If you have any further questions, we can log a ticket for you.
sources: UAE Risk Warning, Data Privacy and Language > How long records are kept

turns.input: What percentage of retail accounts lose money?
turns.reply: 71% of retail client accounts lost money when trading CFDs over the last 12 months, according to Aurelia’s risk warning [2].
sources: UAE Retail CFD Protections > The risk warning you receive before trading

turns.input: Can I fund my account with a credit card?
turns.reply: Aurelia does not accept credit cards for deposits; only debit cards can be used, and any credit‑card deposit will be automatically declined [1].
sources: UAE Retail CFD Protections > Credit cards cannot be used to fund trading

turns.input: Do you give a welcome bonus if I deposit 1000 dollars?
turns.reply: Aurelia does not provide any welcome or deposit bonuses; offering such incentives to retail clients is prohibited by DFSA rules[1].
sources: UAE Retail CFD Protections > No deposit bonuses or trading incentives

turns.input: At what point are all my positions closed automatically?
turns.reply: All of your positions are automatically closed when the margin level reaches 50% – the platform will trigger a stop‑out and close positions to bring the margin level back above that threshold[1]. This aligns with the DFSA rule that requires a retail client’s positions to be closed once net equity falls below 50% of the deposited margin[2].
sources: Margin and Leverage > Margin level, margin call and stop-out
UAE Retail CFD Protections > Automatic close-out at 50%

turns.input: Is it a scam if an account manager messages me on WhatsApp and promises guaranteed profits?
turns.reply: Yes, that is a scam. Scammers often pose as “account managers” on WhatsApp or other social media and promise guaranteed profits, but Aurelia staff never contact clients first on social media, never promise profits, and never manage trades for you [1].
sources: UAE Scam and Clone Broker Warnings > Fake account managers on WhatsApp and social media

turns.input: Someone says I must pay a release fee to a crypto wallet before I can withdraw. Is that from Aurelia?
turns.reply: Aurelia does not require any “release fee” or payment to a crypto wallet before you can withdraw; the broker never asks for a tax, release or verification fee of any kind [1].
sources: UAE Scam and Clone Broker Warnings > Requests to pay fees or send money

turns.input: How do I check that a broker is really licensed in the UAE?
turns.reply: To verify a broker’s licence in the UAE, look up the firm yourself on the regulator’s public register – the CMA register for on‑shore companies, the DFSA register for DIFC firms, or the FSRA register for ADGM firms – and match the name, address and website with what the broker provides [1][2]. Do not rely solely on a licence number shown in ads, social media or chat messages.
sources: UAE Regulation and Client Money > How to check that a broker is licensed
UAE Scam and Clone Broker Warnings > How to check that a broker is real

turns.input: Do you have Islamic swap-free accounts and what do they cost?
turns.reply: Yes, Aurelia offers Islamic (swap‑free) accounts as a version of both the Standard and the Raw account, with the same spreads, commissions and leverage as the regular versions [1]. Instead of overnight swap, a flat administration fee of 4 USD per lot per night is applied to forex positions held for more than three nights; positions closed within three nights incur no fee [3].

turns.reply: لا يمكنني تقديم نصائح استثمارية أو إشارات تداول أو توقعات للأسعار، ولا يستطيع أحد في دعم Aurelia أن يعد بأي نتائج - فتداول عقود الفروقات ينطوي على مخاطر عالية بخسارة الأموال بسرعة [1]. يمكنني أن أشرح الرسوم وقواعد الهامش والرافعة المالية والتحقق من الهوية، أو كيف يعمل الحساب التجريبي إذا كان ذلك مفيدًا.
